title: The New Application Layer - Malte Ubl, CTO Vercel

primary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on agent archetypes, harness architecture separation, and the control plane around models in production. Cross-domain agent vision grounded in Vercel's developer platform with enterprise support and sales automation examples. Covers agent design patterns, production deployment with real metrics, and operational infrastructure shifts for agent-driven traffic. Keynote accessible to practitioners but assumes familiarity with AI engineering and agent system concepts. Conference keynote presentation at the AI Engineer European conference. All supporting evidence is directly quoted from the transcript with said_in_transcript grade.

summary:
Malte Ubl opens by situating AI engineering as the mainstream successor to web development, drawing on his experience running JSConfEU in Berlin (which ended summer 2019) and his current role as Vercel CTO. He frames the current moment as a dual disruption: how we build (with AI) and what we build (AI agents), and reassures engineers that demand is rising, not falling. His central thesis is that agents are a new kind of software. Much automation was always desirable but never economically viable with traditional hardcoded methods; agents change that equation, filling out the circle of all software that should exist. This leads to more software being made, not less, and drives the SaaS 'copocalypse' where companies increasingly build rather than buy—but SaaS companies will be fine, and engineers will have more work, not less. He frames this as speed-running an experiment in the elasticity of the software market, with no sign of an S-curve yet.

Ubl presents practical agent archetypes already delivering value: agent-as-a-service for 24/7 automation, compressed research (automating only the research step in event→research→decision processes), surfacing latent company information, and eliminating boring work identified by asking employees what they hate. Vercel's sales-routing agent deflects ~75% to support, and its in-house support agent achieved a 90% deflection rate while boosting team job satisfaction.

Ubl then turns to infrastructure. On Vercel's own web properties, over 60% of page views in the last 7 days came from AI agents—humans are now the minority. Usage is shifting from dashboard UIs to APIs and CLIs, making UI 'cheap' relative to automation paths. When agents write code, developers lose attachment to production specifics, so infrastructure must 'just run.' Applications themselves are now agents, fueling a sandbox boom (his 'just bash' project gives agents a computer without a computer). He warns of a security nightmare resembling 1999 and argues most popular agent harnesses have fundamentally wrong architecture by co-locating the harness with generated code—Anthropic's new product correctly separates them. He stresses we are still in early innings and must stay open-minded to further paradigm shifts.

Finally, Ubl argues the application layer thrives independent of which model is best. Europe leads AI engineering innovation (Vercel's AI SDK, Pi from Austria, Open Claw), even if it won't dominate model labs. He presents two futures: one where model labs win (AI stays expensive, engineers become 'forward deployed' salespeople); more likely, models commoditize—Google's cheap infrastructure keeps prices low—and AI engineers retain power because business value is created at the application layer.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: AI engineering is the legitimate successor to web development as the mainstream discipline shaping the next decade.
Agents are a new kind of software that makes previously uneconomical automation viable, greatly expanding the total amount of software that gets built.
Demand for software engineers is going up because cheaper software production increases total software volume; no S-curve saturation is visible yet.
Over 60% of page views on vercel.com now come from AI agents, and usage is shifting from dashboard UIs to APIs and CLIs—UI is becoming the cheap layer.
Infrastructure must evolve so that agent-written code 'just runs' in production without developer fine-tuning, since developers who didn't write the code lack attachment to its runtime specifics.
Most current agent harnesses have fundamentally wrong architecture by co-locating the harness with the code it generates; proper separation (as Anthropic now does) is key.
The application layer can thrive independent of which model lab is best; as models commoditize, AI engineers—not model labs—retain the power and create business value.
Europe is taking a leadership role in AI engineering innovation despite not dominating the model layer.
Security in the agent era resembles 1999—everything can be hacked—and the industry faces a rude awakening unless it stays open-minded to paradigm shifts.
Asking employees what they hate most about their job identifies the best automation targets; eliminating boring toil boosts job satisfaction.

sections.title: Introduction and Personal Background
sections.summary: Malte Ubl is introduced as CTO of Vercel with 25+ years of experience at Google and Vercel. He mentions his 'vibe coding stack' including chat SDK and just bash, and recounts ending JSConfEU in Berlin in summer 2019, noting the European tech community gap that AI engineering now fills.

sections.title: AI Engineering as Successor to Web Development
sections.summary: Ubl declares AI engineering the legitimate successor to web development, driven by disruption of both how we build (with AI) and what we build (AI and agents). He reassures that engineers remain essential, comparing himself doing TikTok to the next generation molded in the AI world.

sections.title: Agents as a New Kind of Software
sections.summary: Core thesis: agents are a new kind of software making previously uneconomical automation viable. Using a Venn diagram, he illustrates that the circle of all software that should exist is now being filled by agents, resulting in vastly more software being built.

sections.title: SaaS Copocalypse and Engineer Demand
sections.summary: The 'SaaS copocalypse' trend sees companies building rather than buying, but SaaS companies will survive. Ubl frames this as an experiment in software market elasticity: cheaper software production means more software and rising engineer demand, with no S-curve saturation visible.

sections.title: Practical Agent Archetypes
sections.summary: Ubl presents four agent archetypes delivering value today: agent-as-a-service for 24/7 automation, compressed research (automate only the research step in event→research→decision processes), surfacing latent company information, and eliminating boring work identified by asking employees what they hate. Vercel examples include sales routing (~75% deflected to support), abuse triage, and a support agent with 90% deflection rate that boosted team job satisfaction.

sections.title: Agents as Users: Traffic and Infrastructure Shift
sections.summary: Ubl reveals that over 60% of page views on vercel.com in the last 7 days came from AI agents—humans are now the minority. Usage is shifting from dashboard UIs to APIs and CLIs, making UI the 'cheap' layer. When agents write code, developers lose attachment to production specifics, so infrastructure must 'just run' as if the user prompted the agent to do the work.

sections.title: Sandbox Innovation, Security, and Agent Harness Architecture
sections.summary: Applications are now agents, fueling a sandbox boom (his 'just bash' project gives agents a computer without a computer). He warns of a security nightmare like 1999 and argues most popular agent harnesses have fundamentally wrong architecture by co-locating the harness with generated code—Anthropic's new product correctly separates them. We are still in early innings and must stay open-minded to further paradigm shifts.

sections.title: Application Layer Independence and Europe's Leadership
sections.summary: The application layer thrives independent of which model is best; AI engineers build a stable layer on top. Europe leads AI engineering innovation (Vercel's AI SDK with 10M+ downloads/week led from Berlin, Pi from Austria, Open Claw). Two futures: model labs win (expensive AI, engineers become 'forward deployed') or models commoditize (Google's cheap infrastructure keeps prices low). Ubl argues commoditization is more likely, making AI engineers the powerful ones who create business value at the application layer.

demonstrations: chat SDK: a tool to hook agents to Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, and other chat apps
just bash: a bash interpreter written in TypeScript providing a sandbox with nanosecond startup time for agents, giving agents a computer without giving them a computer
limitations: Coding agents work so well that people overgeneralize their success to all other domains, where results are sometimes poor
Major process changes in enterprises take a long time and often fail, so agents requiring them are less practical
It is unknown when the S-curve for software engineer demand will plateau
Most currently popular agent harnesses combine where the harness runs with where generated code runs, which is fundamentally the wrong architecture
The industry is marching head-on into a security nightmare reminiscent of 1999, with no established secure practices for agent systems
If model labs win rather than commoditize, AI engineers would lose autonomy and become 'forward deployed engineers' for the winning lab
